q: Using the Indian classification of fires (IS 15683 / IS 2190), match the fire (List I) with its class (List II). List I: P. Burning magnesium swarf Q. Leaking LPG on fire R. Burning cotton bales S. Burning diesel spill List II: 1. Class A 2. Class D 3. Class B 4. Class C Choose the correct code:
e: Indian and European practice: solids A, liquids B, gases C, metals D. (US NFPA practice puts gases in Class B and uses C for electrical fires.)

q: Consider the following statements: 1. ABC dry powder is based on mono-ammonium phosphate. 2. BC dry powder is based on sodium bicarbonate. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both correct; ABC powder is the more versatile one.

q: Which method of extinguishing a fire is NOT correctly paired with its example?
o: Starving – shutting the valve on a gas line
Smothering – a foam blanket over burning oil
Breaking the chain reaction – dry chemical powder
Cooling – covering a burning pan with a fire blanket
e: A fire blanket cuts off oxygen, which is smothering; cooling is done with water.

q: A deep-fat fryer in a factory canteen catches fire. The most suitable extinguisher is:
e: Cooking-oil fires (Class F; K in the US) need wet chemical; water causes violent flare-ups.

q: With reference to the CO₂ fire extinguisher, consider the following statements: 1. It is suitable for fires in live electrical equipment. 2. It is safe to discharge freely in a small, unventilated room with people inside. 3. Its discharge horn becomes extremely cold, so it should be held by the handle. Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: CO₂ can asphyxiate in confined spaces, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: For a flammable liquid, arrange the following in increasing order of temperature: 1. Fire point 2. Auto-ignition temperature 3. Flash point
e: Flash point < fire point < auto-ignition temperature.

q: Under the Petroleum Rules 2002, match the product (List I) with its class (List II). List I: P. Petrol Q. Kerosene R. Furnace oil S. Lubricating oil (flash point above 93 °C) List II: 1. Class B 2. Class A 3. Excluded petroleum 4. Class C Choose the correct code:
e: Class A below 23 °C, B 23–65 °C, C 65–93 °C; above 93 °C is excluded.

q: A petroleum product has a flash point of 40 °C. Under the Petroleum Rules 2002 it falls in:
e: 40 °C lies in the 23–65 °C band, which is Class B.

q: Which gas has the widest flammable range in air?
e: Acetylene 2.5–82%, wider than hydrogen (4–75%) and methane (5–15%).

q: Consider the following statements: 1. LPG is heavier than air and tends to collect at floor level and in drains. 2. Natural gas is heavier than air and also collects in drains. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Natural gas (mainly methane) is lighter than air and rises.

o: dust suspended in air ignites in a closed silo
a pressurised liquefied-gas vessel such as an LPG tank is heated by an external fire and ruptures
a flammable liquid is heated above its fire point in an open tray
an oxidiser comes into contact with an organic peroxide
e: Boiling Liquid Expanding Vapour Explosion: a heated pressurised LPG tank bursts.

q: Which of the following is NOT an element of the dust explosion pentagon?
e: The pentagon is fuel, oxygen, ignition, dispersion and confinement.

q: Mechanical foam (AFFF) extinguishers are suitable for fires of:
e: Foam suits solids and flammable liquids; it conducts, so it is not for live electrical fires.

q: Consider the following statements: 1. The red glass bulb of a common automatic sprinkler bursts at about 68 °C. 2. Halon is being replaced by clean agents because it is a powerful greenhouse gas that does not affect the ozone layer. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Halon is phased out because it depletes the ozone layer.
